items.text: Among reviews of adults with suspected sepsis at emergency department triage, what do reviews of point-of-care lactate report about identifying sepsis with organ dysfunction and in-hospital death, how often does a normal value falsely reassure and a raised value falsely alarm, how much do the reviews overlap, and how much confidence do they deserve?
items.population: Adults with suspected sepsis at emergency department triage, as studied in published reviews
items.intervention: Point-of-care lactate at triage at thresholds of 2 and 4 mmol/L
items.comparator: Diagnosis of sepsis with organ dysfunction, or in-hospital death, as defined by each review
items.outcome: False reassurance, accuracy, false alarms, overlap and confidence
items.time: Reviews published to the search date

finer: Feasible with a librarian and eight fellow hours a week before May 2027; interesting to the sepsis group; novel because no umbrella review corrects this overlap; ethical under RO-2026-0907; relevant because the pathway revision needs a rule.
summary: One PICO question with triage-relevant outcomes.
